turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would do as she instructed, but he could not bear the thought of life without her, and that he would struggle to provide for their son and carry on her legacy.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that he must not forget to give the sweet rice dish to their son when he is married, and that it is his duty to see that he is well-provided for.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that he would take care of himself and make his father proud, that he would marry soon and start a family of his own.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked the eldest son when he planned to find a suitable bride, that she might see her son settled before she passed away.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that he would start looking for a bride soon, and that he would make sure to bring many sons and daughters to the household, to make her proud.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told the eldest son that she was grateful for his promise, but that she wanted to see the face of the bride before she died, that it would bring her peace to know that her son was well-settled and happy.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother and father that he would start looking for a bride immediately, and that he would not rest until he found a good woman to bring joy to their household.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan looked at Wang Lung with a hint of concern, her voice barely above a whisper, as she asked him if he thought the eldest son would truly find a suitable bride, and if she would be able to see the girl's face before she died.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he had every confidence in their son's ability to find a suitable bride, and that he would take care of all the arrangements, so that O-lan could rest easy and focus on her own recovery.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan turned to the maid and asked her to go to the village and find out if there is a young woman from the nearby village who is looking for a husband, someone with a gentle heart and a good disposition.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: the maid asked O-lan if she was sure she wanted her to go to the village, as the roads were rough and she might get tired, but O-lan insisted

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked the eldest son to tell her about the kind of woman he envisioned as his bride, so that she could know what to look for in the village.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son smiled reassuringly at his mother and told her that he envisioned a woman who was kind, gentle, and hardworking, someone who would care for him and his family with all her heart.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan looked at her son with a concerned expression and asked Wang Lung if he had considered sending their daughter-in-law, the maid, to the village to help with the search for a suitable bride, as she was already familiar with the area and the people.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would not send the maid to the village, for it was not safe for a young woman to travel alone, especially with the roads as rough as they were.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung why it was not safe for the maid to travel to the village, if she was able to come and go as she pleased

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told O-lan that she was afraid to go to the village alone, but she would do as she was asked if it would please her mother-in-law.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she did not understand why the roads were rough and unsafe for the maid to travel alone, but that it was not safe for her to think that her son was in need of a wife while she still lived

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she must not worry about finding a wife for their son, that it would be done in time, and that what mattered most was that she herself was well and comfortable

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she had lived her life according to the will of her husband and family, but now that her time was drawing to a close, she could not help but think of the future of her family, especially her son's need for a wife.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing she had to attend to before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not speak of dying and that it would please him if she did not.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan replied that she had to die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wedded this good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served O-lan, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe O-lan's face when she sweated in pain. Now O-lan wanted her son to come home, because she had to die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she might die easily, knowing that her grandson was stirred into life and a great-grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they had said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan declared that she would see Wang Lung wedded and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan instructed Wang Lung to sit there and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked if everyone had wine, if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot, if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it, and if the eight fruits were present.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was now content and that this thing in her may do as it would. She instructed her son to look to his father and his grandfather, and her daughter to look to her husband and his father and his grandfather and the poor fool in the court, there she was. And she told Wang Lung that he had no duty to any other.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan said that, even if she was ugly, she had borne a son; although she was but a slave, there was a son in her house.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan insisted that no one else could feed Wang Lung's son and care for him as she did. She told Wang Lung that beauty would not bear a man sons.
